projects.name: filegate
projects.title: FileGate — Naming Compliance Auditor + AI Intake
projects.tagline: Built and deployed an AI-powered data-governance platform that audits about 67,000 client files against policy and files new documents automatically using LLM field extraction.

detail.problem: Client records on the shared file server had drifted from the agency's naming and folder policy, which hurt retrieval and created compliance and E&O risk. No one could see where violations were or who owned them.
detail.solution: Designed, built and put into production a two-part system. The Naming Compliance Auditor encodes the data policy as a machine-readable ruleset, attributes file ownership, locks a baseline compliance score per employee and supports reversible renames. FileGate Intake is an automated document-ingestion pipeline: staff upload a file and an on-site agent uses LLM extraction (Claude API) to identify the client, document type and address, renames it to policy and files it.
highlights: Treated policy as code (versioned JSON ruleset); anything that can't be derived goes to a human review queue instead of being guessed

Ran a root cause analysis on stalled weekly scans: throughput fell from about 178 items/s on the office LAN to about 7 over the VPN. Fixed it with a network gate, incremental commits and explicit failure states, then migrated the job to an always-on host
Production scan: 67,240 items processed in 24 minutes with 0 errors (2026-09-22)
Human-in-the-loop design: unmatched documents are parked for review, never mis-filed
Quality gate: 62 automated tests passing; a 388,000-row database migration verified before go-live
Drove adoption with change-management deliverables: a 33-slide training deck, two narrated videos, a 24-question assessment and two SOPs (2026-09-24)

Added a Scan Dashboard (v1.0 to v1.5, 2026-09-28 to 2026-10-02): a web dashboard plus an on-site sidecar that lets admins batch-rename confidently classified files in place, read client names with AI, limit scans to a two-year activity window and target specific document types
Intake v1.3 (2026-09-30) added a property-folder picker and dashboard admin roles; scheduled jobs on the always-on host now run headless (2026-10-09)
notes: Completed: in production since 2026-09-23. Compliance-rate improvement will be published once rename cycles begin.

flow.note: always-on host on the office network

flow.label: Report + review queue
flow.note: humans decide what can't be derived

flow.label: Scan Dashboard
flow.note: batch rename, review queue, admin actions

detail.impact: Turned an unenforced records policy into a measurable data-governance program. FileGate gives leadership an auditable compliance baseline across about 67,000 client files, targets the E&O exposure of misfiled records, and automates document intake with LLM field extraction while keeping humans in the loop for anything uncertain.

competencies.evidence: Encoded the agency's records and naming policy as a versioned, machine-readable ruleset with per-employee compliance baselines and reversible renames.
Automated document intake with Claude API field extraction (client, document type, address), with a human review queue for anything unmatched.
Diagnosed a roughly 25× throughput gap (LAN vs VPN) and re-architected the job with a network gate, incremental commits and explicit failure states.
62 automated tests passing and a 388,000-row database migration verified before go-live.
Drove adoption with a 33-slide training deck, two narrated videos, a 24-question assessment and two SOPs.

projects.name: uw-triage
projects.title: UW Triage Engine + Board
projects.tagline: Automated the underwriting-notice workflow end to end: LLM-powered triage, a web-based work board and two-way Slack integration for accountability and SLA tracking.

detail.problem: Carrier underwriting notices arrived by email and fell through the cracks. There was no single source of truth for what was due, who owned it, or what was past due, which put policies and client retention at risk.
detail.solution: Built an intake-to-resolution pipeline. An Apps Script engine monitors the notices mailbox, uses the Claude API to extract structured fields, and writes work items to a central tracker. A web-app board lets agents claim and close items, with Slack DMs, a daily digest and commands issued straight from Slack threads.
highlights: Shipped iteratively: engine v1.4 (legacy-notice backfill) and board v2.10.5 went into production on 2026-09-22, followed by board releases through v2.24 (2026-10-22): archive from any card, split multi-policy emails, unresolved-contact outcomes, associated-agent attribution, round-robin and mass auto-assign, an open-cards-only count

Closed a cross-account permission gap (2026-10-22): the engine reads notice PDFs from the mailbox but cannot write to Drive, and the board has no mailbox access, so unreadable attachments stalled cards. The engine now stages each PDF in a sheet tab in base64 chunks and an hourly board job rebuilds it, files it in Drive and links every card from that email; verified byte-identical with a 5/5 test

EOS scorecard automation (v2.24, 2026-10-22): the board pushes weekly team measurables to Ninety.io every Friday (items associated to Sales, Service open/assigned and completed) through a Zapier catch hook with dry-run, push log and kill switch; a close-rate formula measurable derives from them, and eight weeks of history were rebuilt from the audit log
Built two-way Slack integration within platform constraints (polling, since Apps Script can't read Slack signing headers), with every write going through one controlled path
Standardized SLA visibility: one Past Due flag measured in days, plus an end-of-day digest
Regression suites recorded 0 failures at v2.10
Change management kept pace with the code: SOP, Quick-Reference Guide and narrated training videos revised through Training v1.4 (2026-10-15)

metrics.label: Ninety.io scorecard measurables driven by the board

detail.impact: Replaced an email inbox with an accountable, SLA-driven workflow. Every carrier underwriting notice becomes a tracked work item with an owner and a due date, protecting policy retention and giving leadership real-time visibility into what is past due.

competencies.evidence: Built an intake-to-resolution pipeline in Google Apps Script that turns underwriting emails into tracked work items on a central board.
The Claude API extracts structured fields from each notice before it reaches the board.
Two-way Slack sync (DMs, a daily digest and commands from threads) with every write going through one controlled path.
One Past Due flag measured in days, plus an end-of-day digest for accountability.
Shipped through board v2.10.5 and engine v1.4, backfilled legacy notices, and recorded 0 regression failures at v2.10.

projects.name: license-exam-prep
projects.title: License Exam Prep
projects.tagline: Designed and shipped an offline desktop exam-prep app for Florida insurance licensing across six license tracks, then re-platformed it as a web app on the team portal.

detail.problem: Licensing is a revenue gate: new agents can't sell until they pass the state exam. The agency had no practice tool that could run on locked-down, carrier-managed workstations with no add-ins, macros or cloud installs.
detail.solution: Owned the product end to end, from requirements to deployment. The result is a single-file Windows executable (Python, PyWebView, SQLite, ReportLab). It runs full-length timed exams mapped to the official Pearson VUE Florida content outlines, and adds a projected-score gauge, per-domain mastery analytics and branded PDF performance reports.
highlights: Built a 1,467-question, outline-mapped item bank (500 hand-written master items) across six license tracks: 2-20, 20-44, 4-40, 2-15, 2-14 and 2-40
Architected blueprints as data: exam weights are validated at startup, so outline changes need no code change or redeploy
Integrated an LLM (Anthropic API) for AI-generated study narratives, with the API key DPAPI-encrypted at rest and a deterministic offline fallback
Quality gate: 17 automated tests passing (verified 2026-09-22)

Re-platformed as a Google Apps Script web app embedded in the team portal (live 2026-10-19): the same 1,467-question bank ships as a bundled data file, admin tools sit behind an admin PIN kept in Script Properties, and AI study narratives use the Anthropic API; the desktop build is retained as legacy
detail.diagram:
flowchart LR UI[Web UI
index.html + app.js] -- js_api --> API[api.py] API --> ASM[assembler.py
blueprint-weighted sampling] ASM --> BANK[(data/banks/*.json)] ASM --> BP[(blueprints.json)] API --> DB[(SQLite attempts)] DB --> PROJ[projection.py
recency-weighted mastery] API --> RPT[reports_ai.py / reports_pdf.py] RPT -->|optional| ANT[Anthropic API] RPT --> PDF[PDF report]
notes: Question content is original training material written to the public content outlines; it is not sourced from secured exam items.
Logo files in `web/assets/` are neutral placeholders.

flow.label: Web edition
flow.note: Apps Script, embedded in the team portal

detail.impact: A self-serve exam-prep product built to shorten the path from new hire to licensed, revenue-producing agent. It runs on locked-down, carrier-managed workstations with no installs, add-ins or cloud services, and gives each learner a projected score and per-domain analytics.

competencies.evidence: Owned requirements through deployment of a single-file Windows desktop application.
PyWebView interface, SQLite attempt history, ReportLab PDF reporting and PyInstaller packaging.
Exam blueprints stored as data and validated at startup; blueprint-weighted sampling across six license tracks and a 1,467-question bank.
Projected-score gauge and recency-weighted mastery by content domain.
Optional Anthropic API study narratives, with the API key DPAPI-encrypted at rest and a deterministic offline fallback.
17 automated tests passing.

projects.name: training-program
projects.title: Agency Training Program
projects.tagline: Built an internal learning management system (LMS) that standardizes staff onboarding with video modules, randomized assessments, remediation gates and automated manager reporting.

detail.problem: Training was scattered across decks and videos, with no assessment tracking and no manager visibility into results. That made onboarding inconsistent and hard to hold people accountable to.
detail.solution: Designed and delivered a content-driven training platform. Each module (video, slides, chapters, question bank and Core Process document) is data, added through a built-in import wizard with no code change or rebuild, so non-technical staff can publish training.
highlights: Engineered a randomized assessment engine: round-robin draws across sections, with shuffled questions and answer options on every attempt
Enforced mastery: a failed attempt triggers a server-enforced remediation gate, so staff must rewatch the sections they missed before retaking
Automated score reporting to the right manager through Outlook COM, working around a tenant that blocks SMTP AUTH; failed sends queue in SQLite and retry
Added in-app PDF.js document viewing and cross-content search across narration, slides, documents and links
Quality gate: 39 automated tests passing (verified 2026-09-22), plus a Playwright end-to-end suite for the web variant
Web edition (September 2026) moved the platform onto the office file server for use over LAN and VPN; v2.10 merged the sales sub-teams and v2.11 added assignment progress tracking (2026-09-29)

Module library grew through an SOP builder: eight SOP modules (2026-09-25), then Agency Handbook and Call Recording Scoring trainings (2026-10-08); the 'Core Process' concept was renamed 'Quick-Reference Guide' across schema, UI and search index with a data migration (2026-10-07)

Three more modules on 2026-10-23, each with an SOP, a Quick-Reference Guide, a narrated video, a QRG video and a chaptered quiz bank: Ninety.io (my90) for all staff and leaders (32 minutes, 57 questions), the Exam Training Program (19 minutes, 51 questions) and IT Support with Alex (13 minutes, 50 questions); the library now holds 15 modules

Caught a silent failure in the text-to-speech pipeline: two narration clips came back truncated with no error. Found by frame-checking chapter timestamps, confirmed with a words-per-minute audit of every segment, and guarded permanently by rejecting any clip under 1,400 bytes per spoken word with automatic retries

flowchart LR W[Import wizard] -->|PPTX→PNG via PowerPoint COM
quiz draft via Claude API| C[(content/module folders)] C --> M[modules.py
schema validation] M --> UI[Web UI + search] UI --> Q[scoring.py
bank draw + remediation] Q --> DB[(SQLite)] Q --> P[reports_pdf.py] P --> E[emailer.py
Outlook COM / SMTP + retry queue] UI --> S[server.py
localhost Range server for video seek]
notes: `content/` (training videos and decks) and `config/roster.json` are not in the repo; the roster in `koi_training/roster.py` is fictional.
`web-portal/` holds a later browser-based variant (single HTML page + PHP roster API) and its Playwright end-to-end test.
detail.impact: Standardized onboarding into one measurable program: consistent content, enforced mastery and automatic manager reporting, so training accountability no longer depends on manual follow-up.

competencies.evidence: Content-driven modules (video, slides, chapters, question bank, Core Process document) published through an import wizard with no code changes.
Randomized round-robin draws with shuffled questions and answers, plus a server-enforced remediation gate before retakes.

In-app PDF.js viewer and search across narration, slides, documents and links.
39 automated tests passing, plus a Playwright end-to-end suite for the web variant.

projects.name: training-video-pipeline
projects.title: Narrated Training Video Pipeline
projects.tagline: Automated training-video production: turns slide decks and scripts into narrated MP4s with AI text-to-speech and interactive HTML players with clickable links.

detail.problem: Slide-deck training wasn't self-serve, recording narration by hand didn't scale, and MP4 files can't carry clickable links to the tools being taught.
detail.solution: Engineered a scripted production pipeline: slides are rendered to images, narration is synthesized per slide with neural text-to-speech, segments are assembled with FFmpeg, and an HTML player overlays time-synced link hotspots on the video.
highlights: Produced and shipped six training videos in two days (2026-07-14 to 2026-07-15) across three software rollouts
Placed hotspots automatically from slide-shape bounding boxes (python-pptx)
Built in quality controls: pronunciation rules for acronyms and product names, and every segment validated with ffprobe before assembly
detail.diagram:
flowchart LR PPTX[Deck] --> PNG[LibreOffice → pdftoppm
slide PNGs] SCR[docs/narration-*.md] --> SEG[src/segments_tts.json] SEG --> TTS[src/tts_generate.py
edge-tts per segment] PNG --> FF[ffmpeg segment encode] TTS --> FF FF --> MP4[Video MP4] MP4 --> PL[players/player-*.html
time-synced link overlays]
detail.impact: Made training content self-serve and repeatable: six narrated videos shipped in two days across three software rollouts, with no hand-recorded voiceovers and clickable links inside the video.

competencies.evidence: Scripted pipeline from slide deck and narration script to a finished, narrated MP4.
Neural text-to-speech per segment, with pronunciation rules for acronyms and product names.
FFmpeg assembly, with every segment validated by ffprobe before it is used.
HTML player with time-synced, clickable hotspots placed automatically from slide-shape positions (python-pptx).
Supported three software rollouts with ready-to-watch training.

projects.name: audit-system
projects.title: Audit & Compliance Scoring System
projects.tagline: Architecting a self-hosted quality-assurance and compliance audit platform: statistical sampling, rubric-based scoring, issue tracking and BI dashboards.

detail.problem: Policy-file quality was checked ad hoc, with no sampling method, no scoring rubric and no audit trail, so QA results couldn't be defended or trended.
detail.solution: Designing a zero-license-cost, self-hosted stack on the office NAS (Docker): seeded stratified sampling, a versioned YAML scoring rubric, human-in-the-loop checklists (Jotform) feeding n8n workflows, findings stored in PostgreSQL, and Metabase dashboards for leadership reporting.
highlights: Pure, unit-tested scoring and sampling functions
Designed the database schema and migrations (000–003), including a unified issue model for scheduled audits and reactive intake
Built for a hard constraint: the carrier portal allows no automation, so about 30–40% of checks stay human-in-the-loop by design
detail.impact: Brings defensible, repeatable quality assurance to policy-file audits: statistically sampled, rubric-scored and trended over time, on a zero-license-cost, self-hosted stack.

competencies.evidence: Seeded stratified sampling and a versioned YAML scoring rubric make audit results defensible and repeatable.
Database schema and migrations (000–003), including a unified issue model for scheduled audits and reactive intake.
Self-hosted Docker stack: n8n workflows, PostgreSQL, Metabase dashboards and Jotform checklists.

projects.name: pfsense-wireguard-vpn

detail.problem: Remote and hybrid staff needed secure access to on-premises resources (file server and printers), but the agency had no managed firewall or VPN, and staff laptops don't grant local admin rights.
detail.solution: Procured and deployed a Netgate 2100 running pfSense as the network perimeter, with WireGuard as the single standardized VPN. The rollout was engineered so non-admin users can connect and disconnect on their own, without weakening endpoint controls.

projects.name: past-due-tracker
projects.title: Past-Due Task Tracker
projects.tagline: Built a web app that turns weekly past-due task counts from several agency systems into per-agent trends, a Friday manager digest and automatic EOS scorecard updates.

detail.problem: Past-due task counts lived in a shared spreadsheet tab with no validation, no trend view and no accountability for who entered what. Moving the numbers onto the EOS scorecard was a manual chore, and the counts came from several systems, some of which have no export at all.
detail.solution: A Google Apps Script web app embedded in the team portal. Staff pick their name from the roster, enter counts for the items assigned to them, or fill the grid from an export or a screenshot; managers and admins see team trends, a Friday Slack digest and draft Issues for the leadership meeting; the weekly metrics are pushed to the Ninety.io scorecard through a Zapier catch hook.
highlights: Shipped v1.0 on 2026-09-30 and iterated through nine releases to v1.6.1 by 2026-10-14: spreadsheet import (v1.3), screenshot import (v1.4), single-total and separate-box items (v1.4.x), an 'in metrics' switch per item (v1.5), range completeness and an onboarding average (v1.6)

Privacy by design: Excel/CSV exports and screenshots are parsed in the browser; only per-person counts reach the server, with the file's SHA-256 logged for duplicate detection and raw task rows never stored
Screenshot import with Tesseract OCR: every queue column must add up to the TOTAL row, or the affected cells are flagged for human review before anything is saved
Role precedence and effective-dated assignments: Import < Agent < Manager < Admin decides who may overwrite an entry, and switching an item on or off never rewrites earlier weeks
Weekly scorecard push with dry run, push log and corrected-week re-push; Slack reminders and digests start switched off and are previewed before they are enabled
Quality gate: 36 engine and integration tests at v1.6 (24 engine tests in pure Node, 12 integration tests through an Apps Script shim), plus idempotent, editor-run migrations

detail.impact: Replaced an unvalidated spreadsheet tab with an accountable weekly process: every count has an owner, a snapshot date and an audit row, managers get a digest without chasing people, and the EOS scorecard updates itself from the same numbers.

competencies.evidence: Entry-to-scorecard pipeline in Google Apps Script with a Zapier catch hook into Ninety.io.

projects.name: forms-migration
projects.title: Form Platform Migration — 24 Forms to Google Forms
projects.tagline: Migrated 24 business forms from a paid form builder to Google Forms in one day, with a rules engine that rebuilds routing, notifications, lookups and webhooks the native product lacks.

detail.problem: Every agency form (lead capture, referrals, IT and purchase requests, time clock) lived in a paid form builder with conditional logic, per-form email rules, hidden lookup fields and webhooks into the agency's lead platform. Leadership wanted Google Forms instead, but Google Forms has no conditional show/hide, no hidden fields, no per-answer email routing, no webhooks, and its APIs cannot create file-upload questions or set a theme.
detail.solution: Exported every form, question, condition, email rule and webhook from the source API into a versioned JSON build spec, then generated each Google Form from that spec with an Apps Script engine. A hand-built branded template supplies the theme, header and file-upload question (copies keep them; the APIs cannot create them). One submit trigger per response workbook runs the engine, which adds the derived columns, routes approvals, sends branded notifications and posts a payload shaped exactly like the old webhook, so the lead platform needed no change.
highlights: Inventory from the live API before building: 39 forms, 545 questions, 89 conditions, 73 email rules, 5 webhook integrations and 659 historical submissions, every count reconciled against the source product

Conditional show/hide rebuilt as section routing from the controlling question; 55 hidden per-employee lookup fields replaced by engine-written requester, team and supervisor columns from one table; a separate parity audit decoded all 89 conditions
Found and fixed a misspelled notification address that had silently kept every referral-form alert from reaching sales leadership

Worked around three platform limits with tested probes: template copies for branding and uploads, a one-time folder restore Google requires on copied upload forms, and one trigger per workbook to stay under Apps Script's 20-trigger cap
Parity test before cutover: 24 of 24 synthetic submissions and 34 of 34 trigger runs completed with 0 failures, webhooks held back under a test mode

Cut over without downtime: the team portal's embeds were switched the same morning, the old forms stay live through a 14-day parallel run, and five public lead forms that need anonymous uploads stay on the old builder by decision (2026-10-26)
Shipped with an operations SOP covering the template-copy procedure, the folder-restore step and the cutover checklist

metrics.label: forms rebuilt and live in one day
conditional rules mapped to Google Forms routing

notes: Form contents, respondent data and account identifiers are not shown; figures are from the deploy record of 2026-10-23.
detail.impact: Moved the agency's day-to-day forms onto the Google Workspace it already pays for, with routing, notifications and lead-platform integration preserved, a fix for a long-silent alert failure, and a documented path to retire most of a paid subscription.

competencies.evidence: API-first inventory, spec-driven rebuild of 24 forms, parallel run and staged cutover.

projects.name: it-support-agent
projects.title: AI IT Support Agent — Slack and Web Chat
projects.tagline: Rebuilt the agency's Windows 11 help-desk agent as a Slack thread bot and a web chat that troubleshoot first and hand off a pre-filled IT ticket when they can't fix it.

detail.problem: First-line IT help ran on an AI agent inside the form builder the agency was leaving. Its escalation path pointed at a form being retired, staff had to find a separate link to use it, and its knowledge and rules lived only inside that product.
detail.solution: Recreated the agent on Zapier: a Zapier Agent listens to a public #it-help Slack channel and answers in the message's thread, reading the thread for follow-ups, and a standalone web chat carries the same instructions and knowledge base. The original persona, rules and 41,000+ characters of troubleshooting knowledge were copied verbatim from the source product's API. When a fix doesn't work, the agent hands over a pre-filled link to the new IT request form, so the person only reviews, picks a priority and submits.
highlights: Two front ends from one playbook: threaded replies in Slack #it-help for staff who live in Slack, and a web chat linked from the team portal for everyone else

Escalation as a pre-filled ticket: name, category, category detail, system, description and steps already tried are filled in from the conversation; the agent never submits on someone's behalf and never asks for passwords

Rules carried over and hardened: lightest fix first, two to three fixes then a ticket, no Task Manager, security terms escalate immediately, and Slack system notices are ignored so they don't spend the plan's monthly activity allowance
Tested in the live channel before rollout: a top-level-reply defect in v1 was caught and fixed in v2 (thread-only replies), then follow-up, re-greeting and ticket-link behaviour verified
Rolled out the same afternoon: channel opened to the whole team, announcement posted, portal tile added, and a 20-minute training module with seven help pages, an SOP and a quiz

characters of troubleshooting knowledge carried over verbatim

notes: Conversation content and channel membership are not shown.
detail.impact: Kept AI first-line IT support running through the form-platform migration, moved it to where staff already work, and turned every failed self-fix into a complete ticket instead of a vague request.

competencies.evidence: Persona, rules and knowledge base migrated verbatim; thread-aware Slack behaviour with explicit operating rules.
Troubleshoot-then-escalate flow with a pre-filled ticket and a 1-business-day SLA behind it.
Same-day channel rollout, announcement, portal tile and a full training module.

projects.name: website-outreach-pipeline
projects.title: Local Website Outreach Pipeline
projects.tagline: A pipeline that finds Florida small businesses with missing or broken websites, builds two sample sites for each from public facts, publishes them for preview and runs compliant email outreach.

detail.impact: Turns a manual prospecting job (search, check each site, write a pitch, mock up a design) into a repeatable pipeline: one source-fact file per business produces two working sample sites and a personalized email, with checks at each step.
detail.problem: Many local trades and service businesses have no website, a builder placeholder, or a site with broken links and phone numbers. Pitching them one at a time with generic mockups is slow and rarely specific enough to be useful.
detail.solution: Built a screening script that pulls businesses from OpenStreetMap and checks each listed website (reachable, HTTPS, mobile viewport, tap-to-call, contact form, builder, copyright year). Qualified businesses get a source-fact file, and a generator turns each one into a one-page and a five-page static site. Every page passes automated checks, then deploys to Cloudflare as a private, noindexed preview. Outreach goes through a transactional email API with suppression, bounce stop rules, unsubscribe links and a postal address in every message.
highlights: Screened 671 businesses across three Florida counties; 217 listed a website and 175 were checked automatically
Generated sample sites for 65 businesses (130 builds, one-page and five-page), plus 3 fictional demo businesses
Automated page audit with Playwright: one h1 per page, labeled form fields, no horizontal overflow, noindex and a sample banner on every page
Every factual claim about a business's current site is verified, then checked by an independent reviewer before any email goes out
Deliverability guardrails: suppression list, hard-bounce stop rule, sender-domain authentication and a per-message unsubscribe link

competencies.evidence: Python scripts that pull business listings and check each website for HTTPS, mobile viewport, tap-to-call links, contact forms and site builder.
One JSON source file per business produces a one-page and a five-page site with local-business structured data.
Playwright audit of every page plus a separate human-style review of every factual claim before sending.
Authenticated sender domain, suppression list, hard-bounce stop rule, unsubscribe link and postal address in every message.
Push-to-deploy static hosting on Cloudflare Workers with site-wide noindex headers.

notes: Sample sites for real businesses are private previews and are not linked here; anonymized screenshots are in the redesign concepts section of the Work page.
